candidates.title: Fill the context with demonstrations before concluding a large model cannot do a task
candidates.rule: When evaluating a large pretrained LM on a new task without fine-tuning, supply as many in-context demonstrations as the context window allows (roughly 10-100) plus a natural-language task description, rather than relying on zero-shot; expect the gain to be large for the biggest model and small or negative for small models.
candidates.passage: While zero-shot performance improves steadily with model size, few-shot performance increases more rapidly, demonstrating that larger models are more proficient at in-context learning.
candidates.finding: Across 42 accuracy-denominated benchmarks and 8 model sizes (125M-175B), few-shot beat one-shot and zero-shot for the 175B model, e.g. LAMBADA 76.2 -> 86.4, SuperGLUE improves with K up to 32, arithmetic 2-digit subtraction 58.0 -> 98.9, word unscrambling near zero at zero-shot but 37.9 few-shot. On Winograd there was no clear in-context learning gain, and the LAMBADA fill-in-blank format was worse one-shot than zero-shot, and it cut the smallest model's accuracy by ~20%.
candidates.conditions: Base autoregressive LMs, no gradient updates, 2048-token context, demonstrations drawn randomly from each task's training set; K tuned on a dev set where available.
candidates.limitations: Single paper, 2020 base models with no instruction tuning; gains are task-dependent (none on Winograd, near-random on WiC and ANLI regardless of K); longer prompts cost tokens and latency; no matched token-budget comparison against alternatives like fine-tuning.
candidates.validation_test: On your own task, sweep K in {0,1,8,32,max-that-fits} with and without a task description on at least two model sizes, holding the evaluation set fixed, and record accuracy versus prompt token cost.

reason: The paper compares zero-, one-, and few-shot in-context prompting across 8 model sizes on many benchmarks, and runs a contamination analysis comparing full vs. clean subsets. These yield scoped, actionable rules about prompt-time demonstrations, task formatting, and benchmark hygiene. Findings are from a single 2020 paper on base GPT-3 models with a 2048-token context and no instruction tuning, so scope is limited.
